This is the last cluster of the lane's assigned Quiz 23-28 range.

questions.hold: Printed key names Norepinephrine as least likely to cause tachycardia in a recent heart-transplant patient (Quiz 28 Q3: 'Which one of the following drugs is least likely to cause tachycardia in this patient? ... The correct answer is: Norepinephrine'). This is a printed-key/pharmacology conflict: in a normally innervated patient, norepinephrine's alpha1-mediated pressor effect triggers baroreceptor-mediated reflex (vagal) bradycardia that partially offsets its own direct beta1 chronotropic effect, making its net heart-rate effect comparatively small -- but the standard teaching point about a denervated transplanted heart is that this vagal reflex arc to the heart is severed and does not return, so the compensatory bradycardia cannot occur and norepinephrine's direct chronotropic effect would be unopposed, if anything producing MORE tachycardia in a transplant patient than in a normally innervated one, not less. Held per the printed-key-vs-pharmacology-fact conflict rule (same handling as Q19, Q25, Q47, Q166, Q204 in this lane's earlier clusters), not resolved by inference.

questions.title: Dopamine may be used in cardiogenic shock
questions.question: One of the following statements is TRUE regarding sympathomimetics:

options.A: Ritodrine is used in cases of delayed labor
options.B: α-methyldopa is ineffective in cases of hypertension during pregnancy
options.C: Dopamine may be used in cardiogenic shock
options.D: Amphetamine is contraindicated in cases of narcolepsy

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ritodrine, a beta2 agonist, is used to delay premature labor (a tocolytic), not to induce delayed labor -- this statement reverses its actual clinical use.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Alpha-methyldopa is an established, effective antihypertensive used specifically in pregnancy, not an ineffective one.
explanations.C: Correct. Dopamine activates dopaminergic D1/D2 receptors together with adrenergic alpha and beta receptors, including a beta1-mediated inotropic effect on the heart. This multi-receptor profile is why dopamine may be used in cardiogenic shock, supporting cardiac output when it is failing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amphetamine is used to treat, not contraindicated in, narcolepsy -- its CNS-stimulant action helps counter the excessive daytime sleepiness of that condition.

questions.learning_objective: State that dopamine may be used in cardiogenic shock, given its combined dopaminergic and adrenergic receptor activity.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Dopamine may be used in cardiogenic shock."

questions.title: Tyramine releases noradrenaline from nerve endings
questions.question: A sympathomimetic amine that acts almost exclusively by releasing noradrenaline from the nerve endings is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Isoprenaline is a direct-acting agonist at beta receptors, not an indirect agent that works by releasing stored noradrenaline.
explanations.B: Correct. Tyramine acts almost exclusively by releasing noradrenaline from the nerve endings, an indirect mechanism. It depends on displacing transmitter already stored in the presynaptic terminal, rather than acting directly on postsynaptic adrenoceptors itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dopamine acts directly on dopaminergic and adrenergic receptors, not primarily through releasing stored noradrenaline.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Epinephrine (adrenaline) is itself a direct-acting agonist at adrenoceptors, not an indirect noradrenaline-releasing agent.

questions.learning_objective: Identify tyramine as the sympathomimetic that acts almost exclusively by releasing noradrenaline from nerve endings.

questions.title: Phenylephrine causes mydriasis without cycloplegia
questions.question: Phenylephrine instilled in the eye produces:

explanations.A: Correct. Phenylephrine, a selective alpha1 agonist, contracts the iris dilator muscle to produce mydriasis. It has no action on the ciliary muscle, which is muscarinic-, not adrenergic-, controlled, so accommodation for near vision is unaffected -- mydriasis without cycloplegia.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Phenylephrine does produce mydriasis, through its alpha1 agonist action on the iris dilator muscle -- this option denies a real effect.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cycloplegia requires paralysing the ciliary muscle, which is muscarinic-controlled -- phenylephrine's alpha1 action has no effect there, so it does not produce cycloplegia at all, and it does produce mydriasis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Both mydriasis and cycloplegia together describes an antimuscarinic's ocular effect (like scopolamine or atropine), not phenylephrine's alpha1-selective, muscarinic-sparing action.

questions.learning_objective: State that phenylephrine produces mydriasis without cycloplegia, unlike an antimuscarinic.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Mydriasis but no cycloplegia"

questions.title: Amphetamine is used in ADHD
questions.question: Regarding Amphetamine, one of the following statements is TRUE:

options.A: It acts by dual mechanism directly and indirectly

explanations.A: Incorrect. Although amphetamine does have a dual (direct and indirect) mechanism, that is not the option keyed as the tested TRUE statement here -- the printed answer specifically identifies its ADHD use as the correct choice among these four.
explanations.B: Correct. Amphetamine's established clinical uses include ADHD. Its CNS-stimulant, catecholamine-releasing action improves attention and reduces hyperactivity in that condition. This same dual (direct and indirect) mechanism also underlies its use in narcolepsy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Amphetamine is a CNS stimulant, not a depressant -- the opposite of what this option states.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amphetamine has real, well-documented abuse potential, not none -- this is part of why it requires careful, controlled prescribing.

questions.learning_objective: State that amphetamine's established clinical uses include ADHD.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: It is used in ADHD"

questions.title: Dopamine activates D1, D2, alpha and beta receptors
questions.question: Dopaminergic D1 and D2 as well as adrenergic alpha and beta receptors are activated by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Phenylephrine is a selective alpha1 agonist with no dopaminergic or beta activity, far narrower than the profile described here.
explanations.B: Correct. Dopamine activates dopaminergic D1 and D2 receptors together with adrenergic alpha and beta receptors. This broad, multi-receptor profile is unique among the sympathomimetics discussed in this course. It is why dopamine's clinical effect shifts with dose, moving from dopaminergic toward beta1- and then alpha1-dominant as the dose rises.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Norepinephrine acts on alpha1, alpha2 and beta1 adrenoceptors, but not dopaminergic receptors and not beta2, a narrower profile than dopamine's.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dobutamine is a relatively beta1-selective adrenergic agonist, with no meaningful dopaminergic receptor activity.

questions.learning_objective: Identify dopamine as the sympathomimetic activating dopaminergic D1/D2 receptors together with adrenergic alpha and beta receptors.

questions.title: Tachycardia is a selective beta2-agonist side effect
questions.question: Select the side-effect characteristic for selective beta2-adrenomimics:

explanations.A: Correct. Selective beta2-adrenomimetics can still produce tachycardia as a side effect. This can come from some cross-reactivity at beta1 receptors at higher doses, reflex responses to beta2-mediated vasodilation, or direct beta2 effects on the atria. "Selective" therefore does not mean entirely free of cardiac effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dry mouth is an antimuscarinic effect, unrelated to beta2-adrenoceptor stimulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Beta2 agonists cause vasodilation, not vasoconstriction, in vascular smooth muscle -- the opposite of this option.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Beta2 agonists relax bronchial smooth muscle (bronchodilation) and do not depress the breathing centre; they are stimulants, not depressants, of relevant respiratory and cardiovascular tissue.

questions.learning_objective: State that tachycardia, not dry mouth, peripheral vasoconstriction or breathing-centre depression, is the characteristic side effect of a selective beta2 agonist.
